text:
ConocoPhillips fell 1.6% today to $127.30, continuing a broader slide that's seen the stock down 7.3% over the past two weeks. The immediate pressure comes from easing geopolitical tensions: U.S. crude oil dropped nearly 8% last week after Iran and the U.S. held talks at the U.N., and while rhetoric has heated up again this week with Trump rejecting Iran's ceasefire proposal, the initial relief rally from diplomacy talks has faded. Oil prices remain volatile—U.S. crude at $96.41 per barrel today is still meaningful, but the wider gap between global oil ($114.89) and U.S. crude suggests regional supply concerns are moderating.

The stock's weakness reflects a broader trend in energy: when geopolitical risk recedes and oil prices soften, refiners and crude producers face tighter margins and lower revenue. ConocoPhillips has been caught in this pattern all week, bouncing up and down as headlines swing between conflict and negotiation, but the net direction has been down as market participants price in a lower-risk, lower-price oil regime.
